items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1958-08-08; 1958-09-03
items.q: See, Bill Johnson take my place.

ctx.x: Well, they fined Joe $250. See? Joe jumped up and went to pay it, and when we closed there, Joe hadn't paid it. He went away, and he got the man. And I stayed. I wouldn't go back. All of them went back but me. See, Ram's and quit, but Baby Dodds was there. They all went back. I wouldn't go. I stayed. I stayed. And he goes to New York or somewhere. He had then about a 12-piece band. He had a guy. Yeah. See, Bill Johnson take my place.
I started Bill Johnson. So you stayed out here then? Yeah. And who'd you work with then?

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: But they got Bill. Bill Johnson.

ctx.x: And, oh yeah, he was getting $200 a man. A week. In those days, man. So, they find, what did they find Joe? They find, I think they found Joe $500. And Joe, I don't know if Joe ever paid any of it here or there. But when Joe left, you understand? We'd come on back down to Los Angeles. We'd come down there to play two nights for Jelly Roll out to the jump study. Not jump study, Leakes Lake. And we'd play Saturday to Sunday. So, on Monday, we'd all meet up at Tootie's. At my house, you know. We're going, we're…
You know, I'm going to let you talk too long. Let me ask you one more question and then we'll cover. Okay?

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: Joe gets Bill Johnson to play bass with him.

ctx.x: Oh yeah? Garland's New Orleans Jazz Band. Uh-huh. Jazz band, yeah.

Then, uh, Johnny Dodds come in town. We got a hold of Johnny Dodds. Nora Dutre was in the neighborhood. He used to come into Chicago and he'd come sit in with us. So, uh, Boyd H. Williams opened up the, uh, the, opened up this club on 34th Street, uh, Oakland And Joe comes in, all right? Joe gets Bill Johnson to play bass with him. He got a woman named Lottie, she was playing violin, and some other woman was playing piano. Bursar? No, no. We didn't get a whole bunch until we come out here. Oh, I did. First of…
Was it hard to find a piano player at the time?
